text:
30-second contract check before you buy any meme coin:
1) Mint authority revoked?
2) Freeze authority revoked?
3) How many holders, and what % do the top 10 own?
Can't answer all three? Skip it. RugCheck shows them for free. NFA.

Liquidity is the exit door. A coin with $15k of liquidity can't take a $5k sell without a big price drop.
Before buying, ask: how much would I move the price if I sold? Size your buy to the pool, not the hype.

Market cap alone tells you little. A $100k coin with $5k of liquidity is far riskier than a $100k coin with $30k.
Always read market cap AND liquidity together.

Why we show the market cap at every call: so results can be checked.
"It did 10x" means nothing without the starting number and the time. Ask any caller: at what market cap, and when?

Peak vs now: a coin's peak multiple is its best moment, not what holding would have given you.
Good callers label it. Our results are marked as peaks. Look for that label everywhere.

Rug pull basics: the developer removes the liquidity so nobody can sell.
Warning signs: very few holders, one wallet owning a big share, liquidity not locked or burned, mint authority still active.
None is proof alone. Several together is a no.

Wash trading: if a coin's 24h volume is 20x+ its market cap, much of it may be bots trading with themselves.
Real volume usually comes with a growing holder count. Be wary of huge volume on tiny caps.

Take profits in pieces. Nobody sells the exact top.
Selling a third at 2x, a third at 4x and letting the rest ride keeps you in the game when a coin reverses.
Plan your exit BEFORE you buy.

Slippage: low-liquidity memes can move 5-10% on a normal-size buy.
If your wallet shows high slippage, the pool is thin. Lower your size or skip it.

Age matters. Coins under an hour old have the highest rug rate.
Our rule is simple: we skip the first hour. A little patience filters out a lot of traps.

Holder concentration: if the top 10 wallets own more than half the supply, a few people control the price.
Check it before you ape. Several free tools show it.

A call-out is not advice. Even a clean contract can fall 50% in an hour.
Never put in money you can't afford to lose, and decide your exit before you enter.

Why most meme calls end up red: the early move happens before the post reaches you.
Calling after a run means buying near the top. Check the 1h chart before acting on any call, ours included.

What to look for in a caller: the starting market cap on every call, results labeled peak vs now, and the misses acknowledged.
Only winners with no numbers is a red flag.
